### [2026 Usage Policy update](https://www.anthropic.com/news/2026-usage-policy-update)

**Anthropic** · 2026-10-08

Anthropic released an updated Usage Policy taking effect November 12, 2026, clarifying restrictions on deceptive campaigns, weapon control software, surveillance, and high-risk domain use cases.

- Consolidated scattered disinformation, fraud, and privacy rules into a unified section titled 'Do Not Engage in Deceptive Campaigns or Artificial Activity' covering fake accounts and campaign infrastructure.
- Renamed political restrictions to 'Do Not Undermine Democratic Processes' and removed the blanket prohibition on personalized vote targeting to allow legitimate civic engagement.
- Explicitly expanded weapons prohibitions to include guidance systems, control software, and arming autonomous vehicles or drones.
- Tightened surveillance rules to explicitly prohibit tracking individuals without consent, whether conducted in real time or via historical data analysis.
- Added requirements for high-risk health and finance use cases, abusive behavior toward models, and controls for Claude autonomously taking physical actions.

**Why it matters:** The policy update adapts Anthropic's safety boundaries to Claude's expanded autonomous capabilities, specific threat intelligence on AI misuse, and real-world deployment scenarios.

`anthropic` `ai-policy` `claude` `ai-safety` `governance`

### [Introducing the Anthropic Cyber Mission](https://www.anthropic.com/news/anthropic-cyber-mission)

**Anthropic** · 2026-10-08

Anthropic launched the Anthropic Cyber Mission, providing tools, engineering talent, model access, and funding to support cybersecurity defenders of critical infrastructure and open-source software.

- Merged Project Glasswing into an expanded Cyber Verification Program to grant defenders broader access to frontier Claude models.
- Launched the Critical Infrastructure Defense Program to supply Claude models, on-site engineers, and threat research to operational technology (OT) security providers.
- Targeted operational technology environments, such as power grids and water utilities, where legacy systems cannot easily be taken offline to patch vulnerabilities.
- Partnered with eleven founding organizations across consulting, security, and manufacturing, including Dragos, CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, and Rockwell Automation.

**Why it matters:** It deploys frontier AI models and dedicated engineering resources directly to security providers to find and fix vulnerabilities in legacy operational technology before adversaries can exploit them.

`anthropic` `claude` `cybersecurity` `critical-infrastructure` `operational-technology`

### [Building on our commitment to American scientific discovery](https://www.anthropic.com/news/genesis-mission-commitment)

**Anthropic** · 2026-10-08

Anthropic has committed $150 million over three years to the US federal Genesis Mission to expand access to Claude across more than 15 government agencies.

- The $150 million commitment expands Claude access to over 15 federal agencies, including NASA, the National Institutes of Health (NIH), and the National Science Foundation (NSF).
- This initiative builds on an existing partnership established in December with the US Department of Energy (DOE) and national laboratories.
- The commitment complements existing research tools including Claude Science, a 10,000-seat academic access program, the AI for Science research credits, and the Model Hardware Standard for lab instrument operation.

**Why it matters:** It provides major US federal research agencies with computational access to Claude models for scientific research and lab instrument automation.

`anthropic` `claude` `ai-for-science` `genesis-mission` `public-policy`

**OpenAI** · 2026-10-08

OpenAI disrupted two AI-enabled covert influence operations that utilized false-front personas, including synthetic journalists and a fake think tank, to disseminate geopolitical messaging.

- OpenAI identified and disrupted two distinct covert influence operations leveraging AI tools.
- The threat actors constructed 'false front' operational identities, including synthetic journalists and a fake think tank.
- The primary objective of the covert operations was the strategic dissemination of targeted geopolitical messaging.

**Why it matters:** The disruption highlights the increasing reliance of threat actors on AI models to automate and scale sophisticated covert influence campaigns using synthetic identities.

### [ttok 1.0](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Oct/9/ttok/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-10-09

Simon Willison released ttok 1.0, updating the CLI tool's default tokenizer from GPT-4 to the GPT-5/GPT-6 tokenizer family.

- ttok 1.0 switches its default encoding from GPT-4 to the newer GPT-5/GPT-6 tokenizer.
- Empirical testing by William Liu verified that seven GPT models (5.5, 5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna, and 6 Astra/Sol/Luna) share identical tokenization outputs.
- The tested GPT-5 and GPT-6 models matched on all 31 corpus fixtures, returning 44,794 tokens with zero input-count changes for GPT-6.

**Why it matters:** Users running ttok without specifying an encoding will now get accurate token counts for modern GPT-5 and GPT-6 models by default.

`ttok` `openai` `tokenization` `llms` `gpt-6`
